item.title: Likely Illegal Fence Near Daly City Beach Comes Down Today
item.description: A fence that was put up by a convicted felon who claims ownership rights to the property, on a beachfront site in Daly City, is being dismantled today, according to a county supervisor.

item.title: Who’da Thought? Tesla Owners Acting Like Real Jerks at Cow Hollow 24-Hour Charging Station
item.description: A new 24-hour Tesla charging station in Cow Hollow has become a late-night den of loud music, line-cutting, and Tesla bro arguments, and now the station's neighbors are getting exasperated.

item.title: Arrest Made In Rincon Hill Killing of East Bay Rapper After Super Bowl
item.description: San Francisco police have made an arrest in the February 9 shooting of Bay Area rapper Curnal, aka Keonte Antonio Deshawn Woods, on Harrison Street in Rincon Hill.

item.title: SF Police Car Crashes Into Bystander Vehicle During Chase, Injuring Driver
item.description: There was a crash early Friday morning at the edge of Pacific Heights in which an SFPD vehicle collided with a car while it was chasing down a different vehicle.

item.title: Emperor Norton’s Boozeland Gets a Facelift With Colorful New Neon Sign
item.description: A new custom new neon creation gussies up the Larkin Street façade of the popular Tenderloin bar Emperor Norton’s Boozeland, with a neon design that’s actually based on the signature of Emperor Norton himself.

item.title: Trump Administration Insists It Won’t Turn Shuttered FCI Dublin Into an ICE Detention Facility, But Says So in Very Fishy Terms
item.description: The notorious and scandal-tainted former federal women’s prison known as FCI Dublin was rumored to be in the Trump administration’s crosshairs to make it an ICE holding pen, but the administration claims it has no such plans.

item.title: Supervisor Mahmood Wants to Establish a ‘Theater Arts District’ to Gussy Up Mid-Market
item.description: It's no secret that SF’s Mid-Market home to many Broadway theaters and concert venues can be a little rough around the edges, so the district's Supervisor Bilal Mahmood hopes to jazz it up as a “theater arts district.”

item.title: Day Around the Bay: Oakland to Celebrate Black History Month With Black Joy Parade
item.description: MAHA proponents are turning against RFK Jr. after Trump ordered a boost in the production of weedkiller glyphosate; authorities are investigating the ski guide company involved in the deadly Lake Tahoe avalanche; and Oakland’s ninth annual Black Joy Parade takes place Sunday.

item.title: Saturday Links: Two Skiers Die in Separate Incidents at Lake Tahoe’s Heavenly Resort
item.description: SFUSD is expected to announce preliminary layoffs for 42 employees; a celebration of life for Betty Reid Soskin, who died in December at 104, is set to take place in Oakland March 1; and two skiers died in separate incidents at Heavenly Resort in Lake Tahoe Friday.

item.title: Field Notes: BART Poetry, Revolutionary Black Panther Art, and from Rural Alaska to the Super Bowl
item.description: This week: The Dipsea Trail, a crow take-over, award-winning BART poem, and site-specific sculptural CD art. Plus, a beloved pop-up bakery gets its own space, a local violinist shines at the Super Bowl, and Black Panther Emory Douglas’s collage images.
